title: what the comparison finds is what the words say
line: the card, the proof and the hint say what the comparison now finds: Charlotte's 1900 card lists the Residence the page shows and no field for the Norristown it keeps beneath, and once it is accepted the proof says her birth agrees to the month only; a WikiTree profile a name search for John Y Davidson reached, born in another month of his year, is a namesake on the name and the sex alone, never on a year of birth

steps.say: the 1900 Lukens household page, on the owner's word that it is Charlotte's: each Residence it gives shows Norriton Township and keeps Norristown beneath

expect.why: the Norristown the page keeps beneath the Residence it shows is no value of the record's: the card lists it as no field of its own, as the matcher compares none
the census's April 1882 agrees with the file's 12 Apr 1882 to the month: the proof says the month only, never the year only

steps.say: the owner's word on John Y's key facts: his baseline reviewed, his searches open
the WikiTree profile Davidson-349, a John William Davidson born in England in December 1876, as the connector archived it
one of his searches found it: the profile is the search's own result
the profile matched for the person the search was run for

expect.why: the name and the sex agree, the birth disagrees in the month: a namesake a name search reached, no card

has: is a namesake of John Y Davidson, not a card
on no more than the name and the sex, and disagrees

expect.why: December 1876 is not his 24 April 1876: the hint says what agrees, the name and the sex, and never a year of birth that disagrees
